summary.title: Training a Keras model to generate colors
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build a character-level LSTM in Keras that takes a color name as input and predicts an RGB color value.
keywords: color name to rgb neural network
takeaways: Character-level models suit short strings with out-of-vocabulary words, while word-level models can use pre-trained embeddings like Word2Vec or GloVe.
Pick a max sequence length by checking the length distribution of training strings (here 25 characters), then pad with zeros.
Convert character integers to one-hot vectors with np_utils.to_categorical before feeding them to the network.
Normalize RGB targets to [0, 1] and use an LSTM stack with a sigmoid output of 3 values, trained with mse loss and adam.
Predict a color by applying the same tokenizer, padding and one-hot steps to a new name, then scale outputs back to 0-255.
summary.summary: The post builds a beginner-friendly Keras model that maps a color name (such as "keras red") to an RGB value. It compares word-level and character-level language models, explains why character-level suits this task, and walks through data preparation: checking name lengths, tokenizing characters, padding to 25, and one-hot encoding. The model is a two-layer LSTM followed by dense layers with a 3-unit sigmoid output, trained on normalized RGB values, and the post ends with a predict function and links to further learning resources.
